newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank consolidation continued in 1996 - SNB.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank consolidation continued in 1996 - SNB.

text.p: Swiss banks continued to consolidate in 1996 in the quest for cost-effectiveness, but restructuring costs hit their profits hard.
In a preliminary report on 1996, the Swiss National Bank said closure of 19 banks during the year was only partly offset by the opening of nine new institutions.
The annual profit before special charges of all banks combined fell to 3.4 billion Swiss francs in 1996 from 6.1 billion in 1995.

But taking into account substantial writeoffs and charges to clear their books of accumulated bad loans, this turned into a combined loss of 2.8 billion Swiss francs, sharply up on 100 million francs in 1995, with 2.7 billion in 1996 accounted for by the big banks.
Some of the banks decided to take charges in 1996 for bad loans made in the past while adopting "actuarial" accounting methods to set up a reserve pool for probable future losses.
The SNB, surveying financial statements of 403 banks, found that the number of bank branches, agencies and sub-branches fell by 123 to 3,534 last year.
Smaller regional banks were particularly affected by the trend, reflecting mergers to create bigger banks which are generally more cost-effective.
Swiss Raiffeisen banks -- originally farmers' credit banks -- closed 72 offices, other regional banks closed 14, and big banks closed 10 offices.

Swiss Cantonal banks were reduced by one, to 24 from 25, after one of the big three, Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) took over the Appenzell-Ausserrhodische cantonal bank which had suffered financial problems.
Bank offices abroad decreased by three to 102 in 1996.
The trend led to a reduction of 2,024 bank employees in Switzerland. Swiss banks meanwhile increased their numbers of employees abroad by 1,815 to 11,678.
Raiffeisen banks, despite the reduction in the number of offices, increased their number of employees by 162, while cantonal banks cut staff by 881 and big banks reduced staff by 678 in 1996.
